CsfCategory.description: A group of related cybersecurity outcomes within a function, such as Organizational Context (GV.OC), or a CSF 1.1 category that CSF 2.0 withdrew, which the catalog keeps with its status and, where NIST recorded it, where it moved or what incorporated it.

category_incorporated_into.description: The function, category or subcategory of CSF 2.0 that took in a withdrawn category's outcomes, as the catalog states it, such as GV.OC for ID.BE. The catalog names none for some withdrawn categories.

category_moved_to.description: The CSF 2.0 category a withdrawn category moved to, as the catalog states it, such as PR.AA for PR.AC.

category_status.description: withdrawn for a CSF 1.1 category that CSF 2.0 withdrew. A category of CSF 2.0 has no status.

category_subcategories.description: The subcategories of the category. A knowledge bundle relates a subcategory to its category with isPartOf instead.

csf_category_id.description: The category's identifier, such as GV.OC.

description.description: What the function, category, subcategory or example says, in the words of whoever records it.

title.description: The name CSWP 29 gives the function or category.

CsfCategory.title: CsfCategory

CsfElementStatus.description: The state the catalog gives a category or subcategory that CSF 2.0 no longer carries. A category or subcategory of CSF 2.0 has no status.
CsfElementStatus.title: CsfElementStatus

CsfFramework.description: One edition of the CSF as a whole: its functions, each holding its categories and their subcategories.

csf_functions.description: The six functions, in the order CSWP 29 gives them.

csf_version.description: The CSF edition, as NIST numbers it in the publication's title, such as 2.0.

CsfFramework.title: CsfFramework

CsfFunction.description: One of the six functions that sort the CSF's outcomes at the highest level: GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND and RECOVER. Each is named by two letters and described in a sentence.

csf_function_id.description: The function's two letters, such as GV for GOVERN.

description.description: What the function, category, subcategory or example says, in the words of whoever records it.

function_categories.description: The categories of the function. A knowledge bundle relates a category to its function with isPartOf instead.

title.description: The name CSWP 29 gives the function or category.

CsfFunction.title: CsfFunction

CsfImplementationExample.description: An implementation example: one concise, action-oriented step that could help achieve a subcategory's outcome. NIST publishes the examples beside the Core, in its reference tool and its catalog, not in CSWP 29 itself.

csf_implementation_example_id.description: The example's identifier in NIST's reference data, such as GV.OC-01.001 for the first example of subcategory GV.OC-01.

description.description: What the function, category, subcategory or example says, in the words of whoever records it.

CsfImplementationExample.title: CsfImplementationExample

CsfSubcategory.description: A cybersecurity outcome: one statement of a result within a category, such as GV.OC-01, or a CSF 1.1 subcategory that CSF 2.0 withdrew, which the catalog keeps with its statement, its status and where it moved or what incorporated it.

csf_subcategory_id.description: The subcategory's identifier, such as GV.OC-01.

description.description: What the function, category, subcategory or example says, in the words of whoever records it.

subcategory_examples.description: The implementation examples NIST publishes for the subcategory. CSWP 29 says they are notional, that none is required, and that they are not a complete list of what could be done.

subcategory_incorporated_into.description: The CSF 2.0 category or subcategory that took in a withdrawn subcategory's outcome, as the catalog states it, such as GV.OC-01 for ID.BE-02.

subcategory_moved_to.description: The CSF 2.0 subcategory a withdrawn subcategory moved to, as the catalog states it, such as GV.OC-03 for ID.GV-03. The catalog names two for a few.

subcategory_status.description: withdrawn for a CSF 1.1 subcategory that CSF 2.0 withdrew. A subcategory of CSF 2.0 has no status.

CsfSubcategory.title: CsfSubcategory

description: One edition of the CSF as a whole: its functions, each holding its categories and their subcategories.

csf_functions.description: The six functions, in the order CSWP 29 gives them.

csf_version.description: The CSF edition, as NIST numbers it in the publication's title, such as 2.0.
